title: Ask HN: Why aren't maintainers worried about the Copyright status of LLM output?
summary:
LLM output, according to court rulings IIUC, cannot be copyrighted. This should worry both proprietary software companies and open source projects alike (because you can't put a license on something you don't hold the rights for). Yet, even Linux is accepting LLM-generated code. Do they (not just Linux) have a plan?

title: Ask HN: How do you get new readers for your blog
summary:
TLDR; how do you get more eyeballs on your technical blog in natural ways (I'm excluding SEO dark magic)?

Ever since Google Reader shut down, I think the next generations of engineers and developers stopped using RSS feeds. I still use them to this day, relying on a local installation of yarr for my blog following needs.

In the meanwhile, Feedburner is dead, so I no longer track my subscribers (and I know it was always a somewhat noise number) and I've recently installed umami to track analytics and I was surprised when I learned that browsers no longer track the full referral URL for privacy reasons. So I can no longer find out where people link to my blog.

Given the demise of RSS feeds and this obscurity, how do the HNers with blogs find new readers? I assume Linkedin, X and other social networks, but I am finding you only reach the people who already know you. I think planets (websites that aggregate RSS feeds on a particular topic) are also kind of dead, from my point of view.

Additionally, if you don't use an RSS reader, how do you follow blogs of people who you find interesting?

Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50259066
